title: The Faithful Orchard
premise: As the republic of Vessany collapses under advancing armies, courier Kestrel Yarrow is entrusted with a sealed dispatch that names the Halvard family—his own long-lost kin—as conspirators against the incoming regime. Torn between delivering the letter and destroying it, he traces the plot through occupied towns, discovering the 'conspiracy' was fabricated by a general seeking to seize the Halvards' orchard lands. Kestrel must smuggle sworn testimony and the true correspondence to a neutral archivist before the victors' historians can burn the record, sacrificing his own safety and a fragile love with the archivist's daughter, Ilse. The book ends with the truth preserved in exile's archives, the orchard burned but its deeds and names surviving, and Kestrel choosing the record over revenge.
about_author: Marguerite Nystrom is the pen name of a former archival assistant who spent a decade cataloguing the papers of displaced European families. She writes historical fiction about the documents that outlive the people who made them.

chapters.title: The Weight of a Sealed Thing
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. In the besieged capital of Vessany, Kestrel accepts his final courier assignment: a sealed letter to a magistrate in the provinces. He notices the Halvard seal—his mother's family name, thought extinct. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professionalism; he takes the job because refusing means becoming visible.

chapters.title: Which Silences Keep People Safe
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, with a flashback to his three years of courier work. Traveling through collapsing towns, he reflects on the silences that saved lives—including his own. At the first waypoint he learns the letter's route passes through Halvard orchard country. Emotional beat: the cost of invisibility, and the first pull toward his own history.

chapters.title: The Orchard at the Edge of the Map
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse Brandt, daughter of a neutral archivist, catalogs fleeing families' papers in a river town and encounters Kestrel, who asks discreet questions about Halvard land records. Their wary exchange sparks mutual recognition of two people keeping dangerous knowledge. Emotional beat: cautious attraction born of shared secrecy.

chapters.title: A Plot No One Wants a Part Of
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. He reaches the magistrate and, against orders, breaks the seal: the letter names the Halvards as conspirators, with orders for their arrest. He recognizes the handwriting of General Voss, the advancing regime's land commissioner. Emotional beat: betrayal crystallizing into resolve—he can no longer stay a courier; he must become a witness.

chapters.title: Kinship, Proven by Ash
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. He reaches the Halvard orchard ahead of the arrest order and meets his aunt Maren, who confirms the conspiracy is fabricated to seize the orchards. She gives him the family's true correspondence with the old republic. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed—not land, but the duty to remember.

chapters.title: The Historians Are Coming
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Voss's clerks arrive at the archive demanding the destruction of 'seditious' records. Ilse hides the Halvard deeds inside a shipment of mundane agricultural ledgers and sends word to Kestrel. Emotional beat: quiet courage; love against duty as Ilse risks her father's neutrality for the truth.

chapters.title: Testimony Under a Borrowed Name
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Pursued by Voss's men, Kestrel gathers sworn statements from orchard workers and a defected clerk who forged the conspiracy documents. His aunt is arrested buying him time. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into urgency; the record is now worth more than rescue.

chapters.title: The Burning Row
chapters.summary: Alternating Kestrel and Ilse POVs. Voss burns the orchard as an 'example.' Kestrel, wounded, carries the testimony and true correspondence through the smoke toward Ilse's river town, while Ilse bargains with a barge captain to move the hidden ledgers downstream. Emotional beat: climax of loss and flight—everything burning except what they carry.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Kestrel and Ilse's POVs converge. At the neutral archive, Ilse's father must choose: destroy the papers under Voss's order or certify them under neutral seal. He certifies them, and Kestrel signs his own name to the testimony for the first time in three years. Emotional beat: the climax of justice outside the law—the truth made official where no court will ever sit.

chapters.title: What the Trees Leave Behind
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV, years later. In exile, Ilse catalogs the Halvard file as Voss's version of events hardens into official history. Kestrel, living quietly under a new name, visits; they graft a cutting from a smuggled Halvard scion. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—the republic is gone, the orchard burned, but the record and the love endure, planted against forgetting.
